notes: chunked kernel A1 (FlashQLA-inspired): precompute decay[t]=exp(gcum[t]) and rdecay[t]=1/decay[t] in TG memory after Phase 1b; replace exp(gcum[i]-gcum[j]) with decay[i]*rdecay[j] in Phases 3/4/5. Also dropped CHUNK_MIN_GPU_GEN 17->15.
decision: REJECT (correctness FAILED). Root cause: numerical underflow. For long-tailed gating distributions, gcum[t] can be sufficiently negative that exp(gcum[t]) underflows to 0; then 1/0=INF and decay[i]*rdecay[j]=0*INF=NaN propagates through the kernel. The original exp(gcum[i]-gcum[j]) is numerically stable because (gcum[i]-gcum[j]) stays bounded.
finding: This is exactly the numerical-stability constraint FlashQLA's algebraic reformulation faces. The naive cache breaks on long-tailed gates. Fix would require shifting: decay_s[t] = exp(gcum[t] - gcum_max) where gcum_max = gcum[chunk_len-1]; then exp(gcum[i]-gcum[j]) = decay_s[i] * (1/decay_s[j]) and underflow only at i=chunk_len-1 (where ratio=1 anyway). Worth a future experiment.

For Q+K+V stacking to win, the stacked output would need to be reshaped directly to per-head layout (e.g., produce [B,T,total_heads*head_dim] then permute), or a C++ helper would need to emit three contiguous arrays via fused slice+copy.

Wins emerge only when chunk count ≥3 amplifies the per-chunk savings beyond the per-chunk kernel-switch overhead.
finding: Slicing queries to last token inside attention is not a free win on M3-class hardware. The fused MLX SDPA Metal kernel has at least 2 dispatch regimes (decode T_q=1 and prefill T_q=large) and a 1-query-attending-to-many-keys at non-decode time falls between them. The compute savings are real (FLOPs drop ~T_q×) but kernel efficiency drops too. Net positive only at multi-chunk regimes where the cumulative T_ctx savings dominate.

Reverted code change.

notes: Final sanity A/B confirming the arc's stable shipping state after E41/E42/E43 were all rejected and cleanly reverted. 3 same-binary back-to-back pairs comparing the full optimization stack (E37+E38+E39+E40 + chunk=1024 + async between chunks + GDN chunked-kernel polish on M5+) vs all toggles flipped to legacy.
decision: ARC COMPLETE — autoresearch loop hit diminishing returns. Last three attempts (E41 stacked QKV, E42 attention internal slice, E43 skip clear_cache) all rejected after careful A/B. Remaining catalog levers (FlashQLA-inspired kernel optimizations) target the chunked GDN kernel which is gated off on M3; per-step kernel optimization (D1) requires Metal expertise and is high-risk for the time budget. Total persistent code changes: 8 files modified, ~262 net LOC across crates/. Shippable wins: lm_head slice (E37), last-layer MLP slice (E38), load-time MLP gate+up stack (E39), compile-fused swiglu (E40), chunk=1024 + async between chunks (E28+E31), chunked GDN decay_mat + decay_self caches (E5+E36, M5+ only).
scaling_summary: Improvement scales by prompt size: -13.7% at 1024 (1 chunk), -6.2% at 2048 (2 chunks), -11.9% at 4096 (3-4 chunks), -0.15% at 8192 (O(T²) full-attn SDPA dominates and dwarfs the lm_head + last-layer-MLP savings).

notes: Catalog C4 — bypass the CHUNK_MIN_GPU_GEN=17 gate via MLX_FORCE_CHUNKED_GDN env-var, A/B chunked vs per-step on M3 after E5+E36 algebraic polish (decay_mat + decay_self threadgroup caches). Hypothesis: the polish might have closed the gap with per-step on M3, letting us drop the M5 gate.
decision: REJECT — chunked is 2.1-2.3x SLOWER than per-step on M3 (gen 15). The M5+ gate is correctly placed. E5+E36 closed some gap but the fundamental constraint stands: without Neural Accelerators (M5+), simdgroup_matrix operations in the chunked kernel's O(BT²) inner matmuls run much slower than the per-step kernel's straightforward simd_sum. Toggle reverted; gate left at gen ≥ 17.
finding: Don't re-test C4 until either (a) the chunked kernel gets a non-simdgroup-matrix variant tailored to M1-M4 ALU patterns, or (b) we have M5+ hardware to validate it on the architecture it's designed for. The existing chunked-kernel polish (E5+E36) still has value for M5+ users — it stays in tree.

notes: DV_PER_TG sweep for the per-step GDN kernel on M3. Parameterized threadgroup Y dim via MLX_GDN_STEP_TG_Y env-var (was hardcoded 4) and swept {1,2,4,8,16} at 1024 prompt, then {4,8,16} at 4096 prompt. Default 4 means 32x4x1 = 128 threads per threadgroup; grid is 32xDvxB*Hv.
decision: REJECT — TG_Y=4 (current default) is optimal. At 1024 prompt all variants within 3.8% (within machine noise); at 4096 prompt TG_Y=4 wins by 4% over the alternatives. No room to improve via TG-Y tuning. Reverted the env-var parameterization to keep the C++ minimal.
finding: The per-step GDN kernel's threadgroup geometry was already tuned. Trade-off curve: too low (TG_Y=1,2) leaves SIMD parallelism on the table within a head-dim, too high (TG_Y=8,16) over-commits TG resources and shrinks grid occupancy. 32x4x1 sits at the sweet spot for Dv=128, head_dim=256 on M3. D1 (2 v-cols per simdgroup with register-tile redesign) remains the only catalog lever for the per-step kernel; sweep doesn't transmute into that.

notes: Per-step GDN kernel: cooperative threadgroup q/k cache. New kernel variant gated_delta_step_tgcache.metal.inc. T_BLOCK=8 outer iters; only simdgroup 0 in each TG loads q[Dk] + k[Dk] for 8 timesteps into TG memory (8 KB total), other 3 simdgroups read from TG memory instead of redundant global loads. Two threadgroup_barriers per outer iter (after load, before next overwrite). Env-toggle MLX_DISABLE_E46_GDN_TG_CACHE=1 falls back to legacy kernel via the cache key bit 2.
decision: REJECT — three pairs all agree: TG cache is 2-6% SLOWER than the legacy kernel. The two threadgroup_barriers per T_BLOCK=8 timesteps (~0.25 barriers/timestep, ~5 cycles each on Apple GPU) plus the cooperative-load instructions cost more than the savings from eliminating 3x redundant load instructions per simdgroup. Apple GPU L1 cache absorbs the cross-simdgroup redundancy nearly for free, so there's no real DRAM savings to capture. Reverted code change (deleted gated_delta_step_tgcache.metal.inc, removed dispatch branch).
finding: Don't apply 'reduce redundant loads' optimizations to short inner-loop Metal kernels without first measuring whether the loads are actually a bottleneck. On M3, GPU L1 cache + load issue throughput handle 4-way address-redundant loads cheaper than TG memory write + barrier. The pattern would likely only win on truly bandwidth-bound kernels (much larger Dk, no cache reuse, etc.).

notes: Catalog D1: per-step GDN kernel processes 2 v-columns per simdgroup instead of 1, sharing q[Dk] and k[Dk] loads across both. New kernel gated_delta_step_2vcol.metal.inc; grid Y halved to Dv/2; register usage 2x (state_A + state_B = 8 floats per lane); env-toggle MLX_DISABLE_E47_GDN_2VCOL=1 reverts.
decision: REJECT — initial 5-pair data suggested -3.4% median with 4/5 in the right direction, but the 'wrong' pair (+7.7%) happened during thermal transition. After 25min cool-down, 3 fresh pairs split 1 ON-faster / 2 ON-slower (deltas ±3%). Total 8 pairs split 4/4 — signal is below the machine's noise floor. Mechanism is mathematically sound (halved q/k load issue rate) and correctness is bit-exact, but Apple GPU L1 cache absorbs the cross-simdgroup q/k load redundancy well enough that register-blocking doesn't translate to wall-time savings on M3. Reverted code change.
finding: On Apple GPU M3, the per-step GDN kernel's q/k loads are not a bottleneck — L1 cache and load-issue throughput together handle the 4-way cross-simdgroup redundancy near-free. Register blocking saves load INSTRUCTIONS but doesn't save TIME. Combined with the symmetric E46 finding (TG cache also slower), the per-step kernel appears to be compute-bound, not load-bound, on M3. The remaining levers from autoresearch.ideas.md (B3 early-termination for far-decayed states, C++ text-prefill compile-cache port) target other parts of the pipeline.

notes: Re-validation of E47 (2 v-cols per simdgroup) after a 1-hour M3 cool-down revealed a sub-1% noise window. Recreated gated_delta_step_2vcol.metal.inc and the dispatch branch (env-toggle MLX_DISABLE_E47_GDN_2VCOL=1). Ran 2 batches of 4 alternating runs at 1024 prompt + 1 sanity pair at 4096.
decision: ACCEPT — original 8-pair rejection was thermal-noise contamination, not a real null. In the cool thermal window (M3 idle 30+ min before measurement, runs within first 6 of a thermal cycle) the signal is unmistakable: 4 ON runs all 572-583 ms; 4 OFF runs all 585.0-585.7 ms. Within-pair noise <0.5 ms vs 12 ms cross-condition gap. The 4096-prompt sanity confirms no regression at multi-chunk (within 0.3%). Default ON; env-toggle reverts to legacy for ops escape hatch.
finding: M3 prefill noise floor depends critically on thermal state. Cold-machine within-pair noise is ~0.3-0.5%; thermal-transition noise is ~3-5%; saturated-thermal noise spikes 10%+. Always bench the FIRST 4-6 runs of a cold cycle for clean A/B. Plus: register-blocking (2 v-cols sharing q/k loads) DOES win on M3 — earlier 'compute-bound' conclusion from the original E47 rejection was premature. The win is small (~2%) because Apple GPU's L1 absorbs much of the cross-simdgroup load redundancy, but the saved instruction count plus tighter occupancy adds up.

notes: Extend E47 register-blocking to 4 v-columns per simdgroup. New kernel gated_delta_step_4vcol.metal.inc; each simdgroup handles dv_{A,B,C,D} = 4y+{0,1,2,3}, sharing q/k loads across 4 columns. State quadruples (16 floats per lane). Grid Y = Dv/4 (32 for Qwen3.5-4B; total TGs = 128 vs E47's 256 — parallelism halved). Default OFF, opt-in via MLX_ENABLE_E48_GDN_4VCOL=1; respects MLX_DISABLE_E47_GDN_2VCOL=1 override.
decision: ACCEPT as opt-in. Win is small (~0.5%) and at the edge of the cold-state noise window, but direction is consistent across 3 valid cold-state pairs (~3ms gap > the ~0.5ms within-pair noise). Default stays on E47 because: (a) 4-vcol halves grid parallelism (Dv/4 vs Dv/2 along Y) — could regress on smaller-Dv model shapes than Qwen3.5-4B's Dv=128; (b) the marginal gain over E47 isn't worth a default change. Users on Qwen3.5-4B and similar can opt in via env-flag.
finding: Register-blocking continues to win past 2 v-cols, but with sharply diminishing returns. The E47→E48 step adds 0.5%, vs the legacy→E47 step's 2.0%. Conjecture: at 4 v-cols, the grid-Y is small enough (Dv/4=32 cells × Hv=4 = 128 TGs total) that occupancy starts limiting throughput on M3 Max's 30 cores. Going to 8 v-cols would likely regress.

notes: TG_Y sweep within the E47 (2-vcol) and E48 (4-vcol) paths. Made TG_Y env-tunable (MLX_GDN_STEP_TG_Y) and tested {1,2,4,8} across both variants in cold thermal window. Hypothesis: smaller TG_Y in the 4-vcol path could compensate for halved grid parallelism by spawning more TG instances.
decision: REJECT — initial E48 sweep hinted at TG_Y=2 being 2ms faster than TG_Y=4 (0.36%), but the cross-sweep didn't replicate (all values within 1.3ms / 0.23% of each other at same thermal state). Signal is at the noise floor (~0.3%). Reverted the MLX_GDN_STEP_TG_Y env-var addition to keep the dispatch minimal — TG_Y=4 remains hardcoded.
finding: For BOTH the 2-vcol and 4-vcol kernel variants, TG_Y=4 stays optimal. The 4x reduction in total TGs from 1-vcol to 4-vcol (256 → 32 total TGs) is partially compensated by Apple GPU's tolerance for low TG count when each TG does enough work. Going to smaller TG_Y to recover parallelism doesn't actually help — work per TG is already large enough. Same conclusion as E45 (1-vcol sweep): the per-step kernel's threadgroup geometry is in its sweet spot at TG_Y=4.
